roundNote: Round 7 tests the fix for round 6's finding. 7ab3f40f makes Dispatch's createVersionTable widen schema_migrations.version only when the loaded set holds a version above int4, as the daemon already does. Since round 6 it changes only packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/store.go, cmd/dispatch/README.md and the changelog fragment, so round 6's daemon, merge-order, duplicate-identifier and unchanged-file proofs still apply. I re-ran the Dispatch ones on branches built off this head.

implementerProof.how: I drove the rolling deploy myself on my own PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector 0.8.7 (127.0.0.1:55433, UTF8, separate data directory). The drivers call Dispatch's real store.Open, Migrate and Pool.Healthy. They are built from main 2b427f930eac, this head 7ab3f40f, a B-only tree and a merged tree; the branches and the merge are made off this head in a scratch clone. My counts differ from the implementer's (25 against 41 reads) because my loop polls every 200 ms. The results agree: 0 failed on both steps, and 1 failed when main's pods face a release with timestamped migrations directly. The red test passes with its file unchanged since 017d1df01dcb.

proof.criterion: After the version columns widen from int4 to bigint, no prepared or cached read of them fails, including old pods' open connections during a rolling deploy (architect, Envoy c4f2e430; round 6's finding)
proof.surface: Dispatch's real Migrate and Pool.Healthy, from binaries built at main, this head and a later release made off this head with two timestamped migrations, on one database; the old process probes Healthy every 200 ms while the next release boots
proof.command: database x_path seeded by main's Migrate; dispatch-main loop 5 s while dispatch-head migrate runs on it; then dispatch-head loop 5 s while dispatch-ab (merged tree: 20261029200000, 20261029210000) migrate runs on it
proof.observed: main's pods while this release boots: 25 clean reads, 0 failed; the new boot reports column=integer, rows=140, Healthy=140. This release's pods while the later release boots: 25 clean, 0 failed; the later boot reports column=bigint, rows=142, both timestamps recorded x1
proof.negativeControl: main's pods while that later release boots directly (skipping this release), on database x_skip: 24 clean, 1 failed, '22:00:54.339 Healthy=0 err=ERROR: cached plan must not change result type (SQLSTATE 0A000)'. That is the release-order case: the cast must reach the pods before a timestamped migration does, as for the daemon

observations: CI at code head 7ab3f40f: only changes (queued) and pr-title exist yet; no lint, typecheck or test result. 845b318b is handoff-only. At 7fcdf0e1 every job was cancelled by the newer push, but GitHub's router did schedule conflicts-script for this pull request: the job exists in that run's check list.

Release order, for the architect and the reviewer: a deployment that goes from main straight to a release with its first timestamped migration, skipping this one, fails each old pod's uncast health read once (my control above). The same holds for the daemon (round 6). This release must be rolled out before one carrying a timestamped migration.
Round 4's note on the squash body (the commit subjects naming the key) and round 1's note on a PR merged exactly at `since` still apply.
